preamble: In each of a number of clues it will be found that the definition and the wordplay (cryptic/subsidiary indications) do not quite match, differing by one (always checked) letter only, though both lead to real words. Solvers must deduce which to enter. Competitors should submit a normal cryptic clue to replace the asterisked definition at 12.

clue.text: Bad-tempered look when imbibing gin

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: to spy is to look

explanation.surface: A drinker's sour expression as the gin goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the preamble's mismatched clues: 'Bad-tempered' defines STROPPY, but the wordplay builds STRAPPY, one letter different, and the crossing letter decides which goes in. The letters chosen in the mismatched cells spell APRIL FOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition points to the British word stroppy, meaning touchy and argumentative; the grid takes the wordplay's word, describing shoes or a dress with many straps.

explanation.definitionFit: Though, as a conjunction, concedes a point just as allowing does; the grid's word, a feeding trough, is one letter away from it.
